rationale: A wins because it knows where the facts stop. Its customer angle says, "Without on-record access this angle is not pitchable," which is exactly the discipline this announcement needs. B has useful bite, but "A Fortune 100 manufacturer is running Hugging Face models behind its own firewall" turns a cited early customer into a deployment fact, and that is how a decent strategy deck becomes a correction.
gaps_in_A: "The Hub passes 2 million models" as a standalone milestone story — `no_journalist_shape` is mostly right, but A leaves a possible governance/supply-chain lens unexplored if Hugging Face has real provenance, scanning, or buyer-risk data.
"Proof it needs: the named evals and full methodology" misses one load-bearing item: the exact identity and fairness of the "model 4x its size" comparison baseline.

"Next step: `journalist-fit-check`" is a little premature for the benchmark and customer angles; fact-checking the eval claim and confirming customer access should happen before burning reporter names.
gaps_in_B: "A Fortune 100 manufacturer is running Hugging Face models behind its own firewall" invents the deployment. The update says early enterprise customer for private model hosting, not on-prem, firewall, or active production use.
"before it lets AI near the plant" decorates the customer story with factory-floor drama the facts do not support. Manufacturing trade reporters will notice the costume jewelry.

"Hugging Face bets the next AI workload never leaves the device" overstates a model launch into a market thesis. The update supports offline capability, not a sweeping prediction about where AI workloads go next.

"Two million models, and no easy way to know which ones are safe to use" asserts a safety/provenance problem and calls the paid tier a "commercial admission" without evidence. That may become an angle, but only after the proof exists, not before.
